description: Soybean vein necrosis virus (SVNV) is a tospovirus affecting soybean, causing necrosis along leaf veins and reducing plant vigor and seed quality.
distribution: Primarily reported in the United States, especially in the Midwest soybean-growing regions.

host_range.other_hosts: Other leguminous species may be susceptible; research ongoing.

leaf: Small necrotic spots or flecks on older leaves
symptoms.timing: Symptoms usually appear on older leaves but can affect leaves at all stages
plant: Reduced seed quality in severe infections

conditions_favoring_disease.environment: Mild temperatures and presence of vectors favor spread
conditions_favoring_disease.season: Infections can occur throughout the growing season

biology.transmission: Primarily by thrips in a persistent manner; can be transmitted mechanically and through infected seeds (low rate)
biology.infection_process: Virus replicates in host tissues, causing necrotic lesions along veins; vectored by thrips feeding

damage: Potential yield loss and reduced seed quality in severe cases

cultural_control: Remove volunteer soybean and other host plants to reduce inoculum
Avoid planting near areas with high thrips populations
chemical_control: Insecticides targeting thrips may reduce virus spread
genetic_control: No fully resistant soybean cultivars currently available; research ongoing

notes: SVNV is a relatively newly recognized tospovirus in soybean.
Early detection and vector management are key to reducing disease impact.
